title: The Dark Years
subTitle: Chapter 1 – Black
description:
Some people fear the dark.

I don't.

For me, it was always the quietest part of the day. When the sun disappeared, so did the expectations. No one asked where I was going. No one expected a smile. No one cared whether my clothes were too dark, my hair too long, or my music too loud.

The night wanted nothing from me.

Maybe that's why I liked it.

My name is Kael. I'm twenty-two years old, and I live in a city whose name doesn't really matter. It looks like any other city: gray buildings, crowded streets, and people wearing headphones, pretending everyone else isn't there.

Every morning, I take the same route. Every evening, I come back. And somewhere in between, I try to figure out exactly when my life started to feel like a repetition.

It was raining that evening.

I stood at the bus stop and watched the raindrops run down the glass. The same song was playing in my headphones for the third time.

Then I saw her.

A girl was standing on the other side of the street.

Black hair. Black coat. Black boots.

Standing in the rain.

No umbrella.

She didn't move.

People walked past her. Cars passed between us. But she just stood there, staring in my direction.

At first, I thought she was looking at someone behind me. So I turned around.

No one.

When I looked back at her, she slowly raised one hand.

Between her fingers, she held something small.

A black book.

There was only one white word on the cover:

EMO

The bus stopped in front of me, blocking my view for a moment. The doors opened.

I didn't get on.

When the bus pulled away, the girl was gone.

I looked across the street.

Only the black book remained.

Lying on the wet pavement.

I don't know why I crossed the street. Maybe it was curiosity. Maybe I should have just walked away.

But a few moments later, I was holding the book in my hands.

It was completely dry.

Not a single drop of rain touched the black cover.

That was the moment I should have dropped it.

I should have turned around.

I should have gone home and forgotten that evening ever happened.

But I didn't.

I opened the book.

And even though I had no idea what was waiting for me inside, I already knew one thing:

I should never have opened it.

title: The Beautiful Sylth
subTitle: Chapter 1 – Sylth
description:
Everyone thought Sylth was beautiful.

That was the first thing I noticed about her.

Not her long, snow-white hair. Not her bright blue eyes. Not even the fact that I had never seen her before.

It was the other people.

They were staring at her.

All of them.

The man behind the counter forgot to hand back the change. Two girls by the window fell silent in the middle of their conversation. Even the woman talking on her phone slowly lowered it.

Sylth didn't seem to notice.

She walked through the small café as if no one else were there. Her long white hair fell over her shoulders and looked almost silver in the warm light of the café.

Then she sat down at my table.

Just like that.

"You're not staring at me," she said.

I took one of my earbuds out.

"Should I?"

For the first time, she smiled.

It wasn't a friendly smile.

It was more like the smile of someone who had finally found something they had been searching for a long time.

"Interesting," she said.

I looked around. The other guests were still watching us.

"Do you know all these people?"

"No."

"Then why are they looking at you like that?"

Sylth tilted her head slightly.

"What do you see when you look at me?"

The question came so suddenly that I laughed.

"A woman who sat down at my table without asking."

Her smile disappeared.

"No," she said quietly. "What do I look like?"

Now I looked at her more closely.

Snow-white hair. Pale skin. Deep blue eyes. An elegant black coat, even though it was unusually warm outside.

There was something royal about her. Not because of a crown or expensive jewelry. It was the way she sat there. Straight, calm, and completely at ease, as if every place she entered belonged to her for a moment.

Pretty wasn't really the right word for her.

She was beautiful.

But not in a way that explained why an entire room had suddenly stopped behaving normally.

"Normal," I said.

Sylth froze.

For the first time, she no longer looked confident.

Her blue eyes narrowed slightly.

"That's impossible."

Behind us, a cup fell to the floor.

No one reacted.

They were all still staring at Sylth.

She leaned across the table toward me.

"We need to get out of here."

"Why?"

Her eyes slowly moved across the room.

"Because they've been looking at me for too long."

At that moment, the man behind the counter stood up.

Then the two girls by the window.

Then the woman with the phone.

One by one, the people in the café rose to their feet.

No one said a word.

Sylth grabbed my hand.

Her fingers were ice-cold.

"Run."

And suddenly I knew that Sylth wasn't the one I should be afraid of.

title: The Epic Battle
subTitle: Chapter 1 – Antunes vs. Xenthas
description:
The sky above Valthera was red.

Not from the sunset.

From the fire.

Antunes stood alone in the shattered courtyard before the old royal palace. Around him lay rubble, collapsed pillars, and the smoking remains of houses that had still been standing only a few hours ago.

He breathed heavily.

In his right hand, he held his sword. The blade was covered in scratches and small notches, but it was still intact.

It would have to be enough.

"You're late."

The voice came from above.

Antunes slowly raised his head.

Xenthas stood atop a half-destroyed pillar.

His black coat moved in the hot wind. He held no weapon in his hand.

For some reason, that was exactly what made Antunes nervous.

"I had to fight my way through your people first," Antunes said.

Xenthas smiled.

"My people?"

He jumped from the pillar.

As his feet touched the ground, cracks spread across the stone beneath him.

Antunes immediately raised his sword.

"They weren't my people," Xenthas said. "They were a test."

"For what?"

"To find out whether you could even make it this far."

Antunes pointed the tip of his sword at him.

"Then you have your answer."

For a moment, neither of them spoke.

Then Xenthas vanished.

Antunes' eyes widened.

Too late.

A devastating blow struck him from the side.

He was thrown several meters through the air and crashed into a broken wall. Stones broke loose above him and slammed into the ground beside his body.

Antunes groaned and tried to get back to his feet.

"That was disappointing," Xenthas said.

Antunes slowly stood. Blood ran from his lip.

He wiped it away with the back of his hand.

"I wasn't ready."

Xenthas raised an eyebrow.

"That's usually not a very good excuse in a fight."

He vanished again.

This time, Antunes was ready.

Metal flashed.

His sword struck Xenthas' arm.

But instead of blood, black sparks scattered through the air.

Antunes jumped back.

"What are you?"

Xenthas looked at the small cut on his arm.

Before Antunes' eyes, the wound closed within seconds.

"You really came all this way without knowing?"

Black smoke gathered around Xenthas' right hand. It thickened, grew darker, and slowly took on a solid form.

A long black blade appeared.

Antunes tightened his grip on his sword.

"Then I'll find out for myself."

He charged forward.

Their blades collided.

The impact echoed across the entire courtyard. The few remaining windows of the palace shattered at once.

Antunes attacked again.

Left.

Right.

From above.

Xenthas blocked every single strike without taking even one step back.

Then he grinned.

"Faster."

Antunes clenched his teeth and attacked again.

Xenthas blocked.

"Faster."

Another attack.

Blocked again.

"Faster."

Antunes roared and struck with all his strength.

Xenthas caught the blade with one hand.

Antunes froze.

Xenthas looked at the sword, then into Antunes' eyes.

"Is that," he said calmly, "all you've got?"

Black energy exploded between them.

Antunes was thrown backward. His sword flew from his hand and slid across the shattered stone floor.

Xenthas slowly walked toward him.

"You trained for years."

One step.

"You left your home behind."

Another step.

"You lost friends."

Antunes pressed his hands against the ground and tried to stand. His arms trembled beneath his own weight.

"And yet," Xenthas said, "you can't even hurt me."

He stopped in front of Antunes.

The black blade appeared in his hand once more.

"Somehow, I expected more."

Antunes looked toward his sword.

It lay several meters away.

Too far.

Xenthas raised his blade.

Antunes closed his eyes.

Then he heard something.

A quiet whisper.

Get up.

Antunes opened his eyes.

A faint blue light appeared beneath his skin.

Xenthas stopped.

For the first time, his smile disappeared.

Antunes looked at his hands.

Glowing blue lines spread across his arms. With every heartbeat, they grew brighter.

The ground beneath him began to tremble.

His sword moved.

At first, only a few centimeters.

Then it lifted from the ground.

Xenthas took a step back.

The sword shot through the air and landed in Antunes' outstretched hand.

Slowly, Antunes stood.

The blade now glowed with the same intense blue light as the lines across his arms.

"Interesting," Xenthas murmured.

Antunes raised his sword.

"You wanted faster?"

He vanished.

Xenthas' eyes widened.

Antunes appeared behind him.

Silence.

For a moment, nothing happened.

Then Xenthas' coat tore open.

A thin cut appeared across his chest.

A single drop of blood fell to the ground.

Then another.

Xenthas touched the wound and stared at the blood on his fingers.

And began to laugh.

Antunes turned toward him.

"What's so funny?"

Xenthas slowly raised his head.

His eyes glowed red.

"Finally."

Black energy erupted from his body and surged into the sky like enormous flames.

The entire courtyard began to shake. Cracks tore through the ground. Parts of the ancient palace collapsed behind them.

Antunes raised his glowing sword and took a fighting stance.

Xenthas spread his arms.

His smile had returned.

"Now we can begin."

Deep beneath the ruined palace, the ancient walls trembled.

Something that had been sleeping for centuries heard the battle above.

And opened its eyes.

title: The Shadow Comes
subTitle: Chapter 1 – Sentros Awakens
description:
The first crack appeared at midnight.

No one saw it.

Deep beneath the ruins of Valthera's old royal palace, a thin black line spread across a stone wall that had not seen light for centuries.

Then a second crack appeared.

A third.

Dust fell from the ceiling.

Something moved in the darkness.

Slowly.

As if it first had to remember how movement worked.

Then two eyes opened.

Red.

"How long?"

The voice was barely more than a whisper.

Yet the walls trembled.

No answer.

Sentros lowered his gaze.

Heavy black chains bound his arms, his legs, and his neck. Countless ancient symbols had been carved into the metal. Some still glowed faintly.

Others had long since faded.

Sentros moved his right hand.

The chain tightened.

A deep creaking sound echoed through the chamber.

He pulled a second time.

One of the links broke.

Sentros stared at the fractured metal.

Then he smiled.

"Too long."

The earth above him trembled.

Muffled impacts traveled through the stone.

Metal struck metal.

Then came an explosion.

Someone was fighting up there.

Sentros closed his eyes.

He could feel them.

Two powers.

The first was dark.

Ancient.

Familiar.

The second was different.

Bright.

Blue.

And newly awakened.

Sentros' smile disappeared.

"Who are you?"

Another tremendous burst of energy shook the chamber.

Stones broke loose from the ceiling. One of the ancient chains was ripped from its anchor and crashed to the floor.

Sentros slowly raised his head.

His red eyes burned brighter.

"Xenthas."

He spoke the name as though he had not said it in centuries.

Then he laughed quietly.

"So you're still alive."

Sentros rose to his feet.

Dark lines covered his body, slowly beginning to glow. Black smoke rose from his skin and gathered around his shoulders like a living veil.

He grabbed the chain around his neck.

One pull.

Nothing.

Another.

The symbols carved into the metal suddenly flared white.

Sentros grimaced.

The chain tightened around his throat.

For the first time since awakening, he showed pain.

"Still the same magic."

He wrapped both hands around the metal.

Black energy gathered between his fingers.

The chamber began to shake.

"But you made one mistake."

The energy grew stronger.

Cracks raced across the floor and crawled up the walls.

Sentros pulled against the chain.

"You thought I would remain the same forever."

With a thunderous blast, the metal shattered.

A shockwave tore through the chamber, hurling stones against the walls.

Then everything fell silent.

Sentros stood in the middle of the dust.

Free.

For the first time in centuries.

He slowly raised one hand.

The darkness around him began to move.

Not like smoke.

Not like ordinary shadows.

It was alive.

And it obeyed him.

Black tendrils crawled across the floor, climbed the walls, and spread over the ceiling until the entire chamber was swallowed by complete darkness.

Sentros closed his hand.

The darkness immediately withdrew.

A massive stone door stood before him.

An ancient symbol had been carved into its surface.

A circle.

Pierced by three swords.

Sentros placed his hand against it.

For a moment, nothing happened.

Then the symbol began to glow red.

A deep rumble filled the chamber.

The door opened.

Beyond it, a long stone staircase led upward.

To the palace.

To the battle.

To Xenthas.

Sentros placed one foot on the first step.

Then he stopped.

Something had changed.

The blue energy from before had grown stronger.

Much stronger.

Sentros looked upward.

"Interesting."

For the first time since his awakening, there was genuine curiosity in his voice.

But then he felt something else.

Another presence.

Weak.

Far away.

And yet unmistakable.

Sentros froze.

His expression became serious.

"No."

The shadows around his feet began to flicker restlessly.

"That's impossible."

He closed his eyes and focused.

There it was again.

Only for a moment.

An energy that should no longer exist.

An energy he knew.

An energy he had never forgotten.

Sentros opened his eyes.

For the first time, there was something in his gaze other than calm and superiority.

Fear.

"She's back."

Another explosion shook the palace above him.

But Sentros no longer cared about Xenthas.

Not about the battle.

Not even about the freedom he had waited centuries to reclaim.

His thoughts were focused entirely on that single presence.

Someone who should have been dead long ago.

Sentros continued upward.

One step.

Then another.

With every step, shadows crawled up the staircase behind him.

"If you truly have returned..."

He stopped for a moment.

His red eyes glowed in the darkness.

"...then it will begin again."

Far away from Valthera, a young woman opened her eyes at that very moment.

She lay in a small room, far removed from war, magic, and the ruins of the ancient palace.

For her, it had been a night like any other.

Until now.

Her heart suddenly began to race.

A sharp pain shot through her right hand.

She sat up and stared at her palm.

A black symbol slowly appeared on her skin.

A circle.

Pierced by three swords.

The same symbol that had opened the door to Sentros' prison deep beneath Valthera.

The young woman touched it carefully.

For a single moment, she heard a voice inside her mind.

"Found you."

Then the glow disappeared.

She didn't know who Sentros was.

She didn't know why the symbol had appeared on her skin.

And she didn't know that something that had slept for centuries had just begun searching for her.

Not yet.

title: Darkness Against Light
subTitle: Chapter 1 – A Fierce Battle
description:
Antunes could barely stand.

His hands were trembling.

His breathing was heavy.

Yet the blue light across his arms burned brighter than ever.

Xenthas stood across from him.

His black coat was torn. Blood ran down his chest and dripped onto the shattered stones of the palace courtyard.

Still, he smiled.

"Finally," Xenthas said.

Black energy erupted from his body like fire.

Antunes raised his sword.

The blade glowed blue.

"You already said that before."

Xenthas grinned.

"I wasn't serious then."

He vanished.

Antunes reacted instantly.

His sword shot upward.

Black collided with blue.

A shockwave exploded between them.

The ground cracked open.

Antunes was pushed backward, but he held his ground.

Xenthas attacked again.

One strike.

Then another.

Faster and faster.

Antunes blocked every attack.

Sparks of black and blue energy tore through the air.

Then Antunes saw an opening.

Only for a moment.

But it was enough.

He ducked beneath Xenthas' blade and slammed the hilt of his sword into his chest.

Xenthas stumbled backward.

Antunes raised his hand.

The blue lines across his arm lit up.

A wave of light struck Xenthas head-on.

He was hurled across the courtyard and crashed into a pillar.

The pillar shattered.

Xenthas disappeared beneath the rubble.

Silence.

Antunes slowly lowered his sword.

"Was that it?"

Laughter came from beneath the rubble.

Antunes closed his eyes for a moment.

"Of course not."

The stones exploded outward.

Xenthas stood once more.

But something had changed.

The black energy surrounding his body had grown denser.

His eyes glowed red.

"I've waited a long time for this," he said.

"For what?"

"For someone like you."

Antunes raised his sword again.

"You don't know me."

Xenthas' smile disappeared.

"No."

He studied the blue light across Antunes' arms.

"But I know that power."

Antunes froze.

"What is that supposed to mean?"

Xenthas didn't answer.

Instead, he raised his black blade.

"If you survive, perhaps you'll find out for yourself."

Both of them vanished at the same time.

Their blades collided in the center of the courtyard.

Once.

Twice.

Ten times.

Antunes could barely see where Xenthas was anymore.

He fought entirely on instinct.

Block.

Dodge.

Attack.

Block again.

Then Xenthas' blade struck his shoulder.

Antunes cried out.

Blood ran down his arm.

Xenthas kicked him in the chest.

Antunes crashed to the ground.

His sword landed beside him.

Xenthas appeared above him.

"You've grown stronger."

His blade pointed toward Antunes' chest.

"But not strong enough."

Antunes looked to the side.

His sword.

Only a few centimeters away.

He reached for it.

Xenthas raised his blade.

"This time, your new power won't save you."

Antunes' fingers touched the hilt.

Blue light exploded around him.

Xenthas struck.

Antunes vanished.

The black blade hit nothing but the ground.

Xenthas looked up.

Too late.

Antunes appeared above him.

He held his sword with both hands.

All the blue energy within his body gathered inside the blade.

"Then let's try it without being saved."

He struck.

Blue light swallowed the courtyard.

The blast could be heard for kilometers.

When the light faded, Xenthas was kneeling on the ground.

His black blade lay shattered beside him.

Antunes landed several meters away.

He too dropped to one knee.

The blue light across his arms flickered.

Xenthas looked down at his broken weapon.

Then he began to laugh.

Antunes groaned.

"What's so funny this time?"

Xenthas raised his head.

"You really think I'm your biggest problem."

Antunes was about to answer.

Then the ground trembled.

Not like before.

This time, the shaking came from below.

Xenthas' smile disappeared.

Antunes noticed immediately.

For the first time since their battle began, Xenthas didn't look confident.

He looked concerned.

"What is it?" Antunes asked.

Xenthas didn't answer.

A second tremor shook the palace.

Then a third.

Darkness began spreading between the shattered stones beneath their feet.

Antunes jumped up.

"What did you do?"

Xenthas looked at him.

"Me?"

The shadows continued to spread.

Across the walls.

Across the pillars.

Across the rubble.

Then everything fell silent.

Footsteps.

Slow.

Heavy.

They came from within the ruined palace.

A figure stepped out of the darkness.

Tall.

Black lines glowed across his body.

Red eyes pierced through the dust.

Antunes immediately knew something was wrong.

The blue light across his arms reacted.

It grew brighter.

The figure stopped.

His red eyes fixed on Antunes.

"So you're the one."

Antunes raised his sword.

"Who are you?"

The figure didn't answer immediately.

Instead, he looked toward Xenthas.

For a moment, neither of them spoke.

Then Xenthas said a name.

Quietly.

Almost in disbelief.

"Sentros."

Antunes looked between them.

"You know each other?"

Sentros smiled.

"Know each other?"

The shadows behind him rose like black flames.

"He was there when they buried me."

Antunes looked at Xenthas.

Xenthas remained silent.

Sentros took a step forward.

The blue light across Antunes' body flickered.

Sentros noticed.

His gaze traveled from Antunes' arms to his glowing sword.

"That power..."

For a moment, the smile vanished from his face.

"Where did you get it?"

"I have no idea."

Sentros narrowed his eyes.

"Wrong answer."

He raised one hand.

An invisible force seized Antunes and hurled him across the courtyard.

He slammed hard into the ground.

His sword slipped from his hand.

Antunes gasped.

What was that?

Sentros hadn't even moved.

Xenthas stepped between them.

Antunes stared at him.

"What are you doing?"

A new black blade formed in Xenthas' hand.

"Something I'll probably regret later."

Sentros looked at him.

"You want to protect him?"

"No."

Xenthas took a fighting stance.

"I want to find out why you're afraid of his power."

The shadows surrounding Sentros exploded outward.

The sky above Valthera turned black.

Antunes reached for his sword and forced himself back to his feet.

Blue light spread across the blade.

For the first time, Antunes and Xenthas stood side by side.

Light and darkness.

Against something older than either of them.

Sentros slowly spread his arms.

"Then show me," he said, "what has become of this world."

Antunes raised his sword.

Xenthas grinned.

And together, they charged at Sentros.

title: The Transformation
subTitle: Chapter 1 – A Stronger Form
description:
Antunes and Xenthas moved at the same time.

Blue light shot across the ruined palace courtyard.

Black energy followed only a moment later.

Sentros stood between them.

Motionless.

Antunes attacked from the front.

His glowing blade raced toward Sentros while Xenthas appeared behind him and swung his black blade toward his back.

Sentros raised both hands.

Black collided with black.

Blue with darkness.

A tremendous shockwave tore across the courtyard.

The last remaining windows of the palace shattered. Stones were ripped from the walls and hurled through the air.

Antunes was pushed backward.

So was Xenthas.

Sentros didn't move an inch.

"Is that it?" he asked.

Xenthas grinned.

"No."

Sentros narrowed his eyes.

Too late.

Antunes was already in front of him again.

His sword struck Sentros in the shoulder.

For the first time, the blue blade cut through his skin.

Sentros stepped back.

Only a single step.

But Xenthas noticed.

"He can be hurt!"

"I can see that!" Antunes shouted.

He attacked again.

Sentros blocked.

Xenthas appeared from the side.

Sentros dodged.

Antunes struck from above.

Sentros raised his arm.

The blue blade cut through his skin again.

Black blood dripped onto the ground.

Antunes froze.

Sentros examined the wound.

Then he smiled.

"Interesting."

The blue energy around the wound began to flicker.

Antunes' eyes widened.

The light separated from Sentros' body.

Like tiny flames, it was drawn into his hand.

Sentros closed his fingers around it.

The energy disappeared.

"What did you do?" Antunes asked.

Sentros looked at his hand.

"I remember."

Xenthas' smile disappeared.

Sentros raised his head.

His red eyes fixed on Antunes.

"That power."

Antunes raised his sword.

"What about it?"

Sentros didn't answer.

Xenthas attacked.

His black blade raced toward Sentros' neck.

Sentros turned.

A single movement.

His hand struck Xenthas in the chest.

The impact shook the air.

Xenthas was hurled across the entire courtyard.

He smashed through a pillar.

Then a wall.

And disappeared inside the palace.

"Xenthas!"

Antunes tried to run toward him.

Something grabbed his leg.

Black shadows crawled across the ground and wrapped themselves around his body.

Antunes slashed at them with his sword.

The shadows split apart.

And immediately formed again.

They seized his arms.

His legs.

His neck.

Antunes was lifted from the ground.

His sword fell from his hand.

Sentros slowly walked toward him.

"Let me go."

Sentros ignored him.

His gaze remained fixed on the blue lines across Antunes' arms.

They were glowing brighter.

Sentros stopped.

For the first time, every trace of mockery disappeared from his face.

"So you really do carry his light."

Antunes stared at him.

"Whose light?"

Sentros raised one hand.

The shadows tightened around Antunes.

"Tell me where you got this power."

"I don't know."

Sentros' eyes glowed brighter.

"You really expect me to believe that?"

"I don't care what you believe."

Sentros smiled again.

"Then we'll find out another way."

He placed a hand against Antunes' chest.

Antunes screamed.

It felt as though something inside his body was being torn apart.

The blue lines across his arms began to flicker wildly.

Light poured from his skin.

Sentros' hand began to glow blue.

He was pulling the energy out of Antunes.

"What... are you doing?" Antunes managed to say.

"I want to see what's inside you."

The light grew stronger.

Antunes closed his eyes.

His heart raced.

Something moved inside him.

Something that had been there all along.

Silent.

Hidden.

Waiting.

Then he heard the voice again.

The same voice as before.

But this time, it didn't say:

Get up.

This time, it said only one word.

Fight.

Antunes opened his eyes.

Blue light exploded from his body.

Sentros was thrown backward.

The shadows surrounding Antunes burned away in an instant.

He fell toward the ground.

But before his knees could touch the stone, he caught himself.

His hands were trembling.

Not from weakness.

From energy.

The blue lines across his arms began to spread.

Across his shoulders.

Across his chest.

His neck.

All the way to his face.

Antunes gasped.

His eyes began to glow.

Blue.

Then almost white.

The energy surrounding his body became so intense that parts of his clothing tore apart.

His sword lay several meters away.

It began to tremble.

Then it flew toward him.

Antunes caught it.

The moment his fingers closed around the hilt, the blade changed.

The metal disappeared beneath pure blue light.

The blade grew longer.

Wider.

Brighter.

No longer an ordinary weapon.

Almost pure energy.

Sentros slowly stood again.

For the first time, he didn't look amused.

He looked surprised.

"Impossible."

Antunes raised his head.

His glowing eyes fixed on Sentros.

Then he vanished.

Sentros threw up his arms.

Too late.

Antunes' blade struck him in the side.

Sentros was hurled through a pillar.

Before his body could even hit the ground, Antunes appeared in front of him again.

Another strike.

Then another.

Sentros blocked.

Antunes attacked again.

Faster.

Harder.

More brutal.

Sentros was driven farther and farther back.

"Antunes!"

The voice came from the ruins.

Xenthas pulled himself free from the shattered wall.

Blood ran down his face.

Antunes didn't react.

He struck again.

Sentros dropped to one knee.

Antunes raised his sword.

"Antunes."

No response.

Xenthas' expression became serious.

"ANTUNES!"

Antunes stopped.

Slowly, he turned his head.

His blue-white eyes stared at Xenthas.

Xenthas froze.

For a single moment, he didn't see Antunes.

He saw someone else.

Someone he hadn't seen in a very long time.

"No..."

Antunes turned back toward Sentros.

Sentros lay wounded among the rubble.

But Antunes attacked again.

Sentros blocked the strike with both hands.

The ground beneath him shattered.

Antunes forced the energy blade farther down.

"Antunes, stop!" Xenthas shouted.

No response.

Antunes attacked again.

Sentros rolled aside.

"What's so funny?" Xenthas asked.

Sentros slowly stood.

Blood ran down his face.

Still, he smiled.

"Now you finally understand, Xenthas."

Xenthas' expression turned cold.

"Shut up."

Sentros laughed quietly.

Antunes looked between them.

His breathing was heavy.

The energy surrounding his body flickered wildly.

"What is he talking about?"

Xenthas remained silent.

Sentros' smile widened.

"He really never told you?"

Antunes looked at Xenthas.

"Told me what?"

"Sentros."

Xenthas raised his blade.

"Not another word."

Sentros ignored him.

His red eyes fixed directly on Antunes.

"That power doesn't belong to you."

Antunes froze.

The blue light surrounding his body flickered.

"What?"

Sentros took a step toward him.

"You have his power."

Xenthas charged forward.

"SHUT UP!"

Sentros looked at him.

Then he spoke the words Xenthas had desperately tried to prevent.

"He'll end up just like his father."

Silence.

Antunes didn't move.

The blue energy surrounding his body faded for a moment.

Only his eyes continued to glow.

Slowly, he turned toward Xenthas.

"What do you know about my father?"
